title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 2.27 (versions follow prime numbers; 227 after 223): the chain of 'why', without genealogies yet. After her paragraph of who someone is, Luma chains as Razar's curiosity asks why again: a relation (what follows the subject, said in two lines or more, carrying a talk the most by her own measure), its first fact, the next subject (the word of that clause carrying a talk the most, not visited yet), asked again by the same relation until a circle, a gap or the end of her room. Her table of what a subject does now grows (it had a cap of 32, against the plastic rule), and every occurrence in a line counts (a genealogy is one line). Stated failure: the genealogies do not come out yet: the relation she picks is the rarest word after the subject (a surname: 'Isaac Hirschowitz', 'Abraham Zacuto'), because 'two cases' was measured as two lines, where Razar's chainer of 2026-11-08, which did answer the genealogies, asked for two different subjects with the same relation. That correction is pending, so as not to correct in circles (one correction, then publish with the failure said). About 4 s an answer; no crash in the test questions. The kernel is unchanged since 1.39. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v2.27: Luma encadena el por qué; las genealogías todavía no salen, y está dicho por qué. Prototipo de investigación.
